summary: This study investigates the developmental specializations of the human fovea using a combination of clinical imaging modalities, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) and adaptive optics scanning light ophthalmoscopy (AOSLO), to examine the relationship between foveal morphology and visual function in individuals with conditions affecting the fovea. The study aims to assess foveal cone topography and function in individuals with a history of premature birth and examine the relationship between the S-cone sub-mosaic and the rod mosaic near the central fovea. The research will provide key information about the variability of human foveal specializations in both health and disease, informing the treatment of individuals with visual dysfunction.
